anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PCA9685PW (U2) has all six address straps A0–A5 (pins 1,2,3,4,5,24) tied to GND, which sets its 7-bit address to 0x40, while its SCL/SDA (pins 26,27) sit on I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC. On the Power sheet the INA219 (U1) has A0/A1 (pins 7,8) tied to GND (address 0x40) and its SCL/SDA (pins 5,6) on the same I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC bus. The PCA9685 block's own annotation, however, reads 'I2C address: 0x41'.
anomalies.expected: The two devices must not share an address on the same I2C2 bus. The schematic's own note ('I2C address: 0x41') indicates the designer intended the PCA9685 to be strapped to 0x41 (e.g. A0 tied to +3V3) so it can coexist with the INA219 at 0x40 on I2C2; the all-GND strap in the drawing contradicts that note and collides with the INA219.

evidence.quote: PCA9685PW (U2) pins A0..A5 (1,2,3,4,5,24) all connected to GND; block note 'I2C address: 0x41'; SCL/SDA = I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC (FCC Peripherals sheet)
INA219AIDCNR (U1) pins 7,8 (A0,A1) to GND; 'I2C address: 0x40'; SCL/SDA = I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC (Power sheet)
PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40 ... Current/voltage sensor | TI INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: Two I2C slaves (INA219 and PCA9685) are strapped to the same address (0x40) on the same I2C2 bus. This causes bus contention / an unaddressable PWM/servo driver, so the PCA9685 cannot be reliably driven and the servo outputs (PWM_0..7) will not respond as intended. (Note: the spec table lists the PCA9685 as 0x40, which is itself inconsistent with the INA219 at 0x40 on the same bus; the sheet annotation 0x41 is taken as the designer's true intent.)

parsed.summary: The drawing shows the PCA9685PW address pins all strapped to GND (address 0x40) on the same I2C2 bus as the INA219 (also 0x40), contradicting the sheet's own 'I2C address: 0x41' note and creating an I2C address collision that would leave the servo/PWM driver unaddressable; this is the most likely anomaly (the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap is a known bug and is not reported).
